item.content:encoded:
I suspect that "salty" was originally somewhat literal in that sailors (and marines) with salt encrusted uniforms were typically those who were well entrenched in their grade and billet. At any rate I personally never heard it spoken by civilians or saw it on the Internet in civilian contexts until recently. On the other hand "salty Lance Corporal" has been in the USMC lexicon at least for decades.

I was an E3 in an E6's billet (which I was brilliant at) for far too long, I am probably as salty as it is possible to be without being a full on shitbird.

ETA: Having read your edit, I see. That makes sense. I still don't like this article…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'd be willing to bet that's convergent evolution- it's a pretty simple expospeak gag.

Edit: if you mean "salty" the resurgence is actually a return to the original meaning: it started out way back in the 1800's meaning somewhere between "having moxie", "being horny", "looking for a fight" and "being extremely rude and abrasive". From there it got picked up by sailors (who got called that a lot on shore leave) and mutated into "tough and jaded", and now it's shifting back to it's original meaning.
